A tradesman marks his goods 10% above his cost price. If he allows his customers 10% discount on the marked price. How much profit or loss does he make, if any ?

q: The marked price of a watch was Rs. 720. A man bought the same for Rs. 550.80, after getting two successive discounts, the first 10%. What was the second discount rate ?
s: Market price of a watch = Rs. 720 After 1 st discount $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = 90}}\% {\text{ of 720 }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{90}}{{100}} \times 720 \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 648}} \end{aligned}$$ Cost price of watch = Rs. 550.80 Difference = 648 - 550.80 = Rs. 97.20 $$\begin{aligned} & {{\text{2}}^{{\text{nd}}}}{\text{ discount}} \\ & = \frac{{97.20}}{{648}} \times 100 \\ & = \frac{{9720}}{{648}} \\ & = 15\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 20% above cost price, but allows 30% discount for cash payment. His net loss is ?
s: Let the cost price of goods = Rs. 100 Market price of goods $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{ = 120}}\% {\text{ of 100 }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{120}}{{100}} \times {\text{100}} \\ & {\text{ = Rs}}{\text{. 120}} \end{aligned}$$ After discount selling price of goods = 70% of 120 = Rs. 84 $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Loss = 100}} - 84 = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.16}} \\ & {\text{Loss }}\% {\text{ = }}\frac{{16}}{{100}} \times 100 = 16\% \end{aligned}$$ Alternate : $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Formula = }}x \pm y \pm {\text{ }}\frac{{x \times y}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{Loss}}\% {\text{ = 20}} - {\text{30}} - \frac{{20 \times 30}}{{100}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = - 10 - 6 \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = - 16\% {\text{ }}({\text{Loss)}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The equivalent single discount for two successive discounts of 15% and 10% is = ?

q: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 10% after allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price. The cost price of the article whose marked price is Rs. 880, is = ?

q: A fan is listed at Rs. 1500 and a discount of 20% is offered on the list price. What additional discount must be offered to the customer now to bring the net price to Rs. 1104 ?

q: A single discount equivalent to the successive discounts of 10%, 20% and 25% is = ?

q: The discount series 10%, 20%, 40% is equivalent to a single discount of = ?

q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 30% above his cost price but allows a discount of 10% at the time of sale. His gain is = ?

q: A retailer purchases a grinder at a discount of 15% of the whole seller and sales it for Rs. 1955 at a profit of 15%. The amount of discount received by the retailer from the whole seller was = ?

q: The marked price of a T.V. is Rs. 16000. After two successive discounts it is sold for Rs. 11400. If the first discount is 5%, then the rate of second discount is = ?

q: Anand marks up the price of an article by 50% and then allows a discount of 20% and sells it to Balaji who sells it for Rs. 20, more than what he purchased for, this selling price is 30% more then the original cost price of the article. Then Balaji's profit % is = ?
s: Let original cost price = 100 units $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Cost price of Balaji }} \\ & {\text{ = 100}} \times \frac{{150}}{{100}} \times \frac{{80}}{{100}} \\ & {\text{ = 120 units}} \\ & {\text{Selling price of Balaji }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{130}}{{100}} \times 100\, \\ & {\text{ = 130 units}} \\ & {\text{Profit of Balaji }} \\ & {\text{ = 130}} - 120 \\ & = {\text{10 units}} \\ & {\text{Profit percent }} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{10}}{{120}} \times 100 \\ & {\text{ = 8}}{\text{.33}}\% \end{aligned}$$ Note: There is no use of Rs. 20 given in the question

q: The marked price of an article is Rs. 500. A shopkeeper gives a discount of 5% and still makes a profit of 25%. The cost price of the article is = ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Cost price of the article}} \\ & {\text{ = 500}} \times \frac{{95}}{{100}} \times \frac{{100}}{{125}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 380}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The difference between simple interest and the true discount on Rs. 2400 due 4 years hence at 5% per annum simple interest is -
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Given}}\,{\text{A}} = 2400 \\ & {\text{R}} = 5\% \\ & {\text{T}} = 4{\text{year}} \\ & \therefore \,TD\, = \frac{{A \times R \times T}}{{100 + R \times T}} \\ & TD = \frac{{2400 \times 4 \times 5}}{{100 + 20}} \\ & TD = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}400 \\ & \therefore \,{\text{S}}{\text{.I}}{\text{.}} - {\text{TD}} = \frac{{TD \times R \times T}}{{100}} \\ & = \frac{{400 \times 5 \times 4}}{{100}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 80}}{\text{}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Charging 30% above its production cost a radio maker puts a label of Rs. 286 on a radio as is price. But at the time of selling it, he allows 10% discount on the labelled price. What will his gain be ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Cost of ratio}} \\ & = \frac{{286}}{{130}} \times 100 \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 220}} \\ & {\text{Selling price of ratio}} \\ & = 286 \times \frac{{90}}{{100}} \\ & = {\text{Rs 257}}{\text{.40}} \\ & {\text{Profit}} = 257.40 - 220 \\ & = {\text{Rs 37}}{\text{.40}} \end{aligned}$$
